hubs.title: Foundations of Life
hubs.description: What actually makes something alive? Start your journey here at the absolute beginning.

modules.title: Levels of Organization
modules.content: Dive deeper into the microscopic universe. Click 'Magnify' to zoom in from a full organism down to a single atom.

levels.title: Organism
levels.desc: A macroscopic living entity, like a human, animal, or tree.

levels.title: Organ System
levels.desc: A group of organs working together, like the respiratory or circulatory system.

levels.title: Organ
levels.desc: A specific functioning part of the system, like the lungs or heart.

levels.title: Tissue
levels.desc: A collection of similar cells working together to perform a specific function.

levels.title: Cell
levels.desc: The absolute fundamental, microscopic unit of life.

levels.title: Organelle
levels.desc: The tiny 'organs' inside a cell, like the nucleus or mitochondria.

levels.title: Molecule
levels.desc: Chemical structures made of bonded atoms, like DNA or proteins.

levels.title: Atom
levels.desc: The base building blocks of all matter in the universe.

modules.title: Is It Alive? (The 7 Characteristics)
modules.content: Drag the items into the correct zone. Let's see if they meet all 7 characteristics of life!

items.name: 🌿 Fern Plant
items.reason: Correct! Plants grow, reproduce, maintain homeostasis, and are made of cells.

items.name: 🔥 Campfire
items.reason: Correct! Fire consumes oxygen and grows, but it lacks cells, DNA, and homeostasis.

items.name: 🦠 Virus
items.reason: Correct! Viruses have DNA, but cannot reproduce without a host cell. They are non-living.

items.name: 🦠 Bacteria
items.reason: Correct! Bacteria are single-celled organisms that independently perform all 7 functions of life.

items.name: 💎 Quartz Crystal
items.reason: Correct! Crystals grow as minerals deposit, but they do not consume energy or respond to stimuli.

modules.title: Scientific Method Lab
modules.content: Design and run a controlled experiment to investigate how environmental conditions affect plant growth.
learningObjectives: Identify the major steps of the scientific method.
Identify independent, dependent, and controlled variables.
Connect evidence to a scientific conclusion.

hubs.title: Cellular Biology Hub
hubs.description: Explore the microscopic foundations of life.

modules.title: Organelle Inspector
modules.content: Zoom in and interact with eukaryotic cell structures.

modules.title: Mitosis Timeline
modules.content: Scroll to step through the phases of cellular division.

phases.title: 1. Prophase
phases.desc: Chromatin condenses into visible chromosomes. The nuclear envelope breaks down.

phases.title: 2. Metaphase
phases.desc: Chromosomes align perfectly along the equator (middle) of the cell.

phases.title: 3. Anaphase
phases.desc: Sister chromatids are pulled apart toward opposite poles of the cell.

phases.title: 4. Telophase
phases.desc: Two new nuclear envelopes form around the separated chromosomes. The cell prepares to divide.

modules.title: Diffusion & Osmosis Lab
modules.content: Experiment with concentration gradients, membrane permeability, and temperature to discover how substances move across membranes.
learningObjectives: Explain how concentration gradients influence molecular movement.
Understand the role of a selectively permeable membrane.
Predict how changing concentration affects movement.
Predict whether a cell will swell, shrink, or remain stable during osmosis.

hubs.title: Taxonomy & Classification
hubs.description: The structural categorization of living organisms.

modules.title: The Tree of Life
modules.content: Click the branches to traverse the biological classification hierarchy from broad domains down to specific kingdoms.

hubs.title: Genetics & Molecular Hub
hubs.description: Uncover the molecular mechanisms behind hereditary traits.

modules.title: DNA Helicase Unzipper
modules.content: Inject the Helicase enzyme to break the hydrogen bonds and unzip the DNA double helix for replication.

modules.title: Gene Expression Lab
modules.content: Trace genetic information from DNA through transcription and translation to understand how cells build proteins.
learningObjectives: Explain how DNA serves as a template for RNA.
Explain how ribosomes read mRNA codons.
Describe how mutations can affect proteins.

hubs.title: Human Physiology Hub
hubs.description: Understand the complex mechanical and electrical systems that keep the human body alive.

modules.title: Cardiac Rhythm & BPM
modules.content: The heart is a muscular pump controlled by electrical impulses. Adjust the slider to see how Heart Rate (Beats Per Minute) impacts the cardiac cycle during rest versus intense exercise.

hubs.title: Final Assessment Arena
hubs.description: Test your knowledge across all phases with this interactive, gamified quiz.

modules.content: Answer carefully! Let's see how much you remember about cells, DNA, and human physiology.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the 7 characteristics of life?
In the cellular Mitosis timeline, during which phase do chromosomes align at the equator?
What is the function of the Helicase enzyme in DNA replication?
options: It unzips the DNA double helix

questions.question: If a resting heart rate is 60 BPM, what biological state does 170 BPM likely indicate?

hubs.title: Energy & Metabolism
hubs.description: Visualize the continuous flow of energy and matter through biological systems.

modules.title: Photosynthesis Reaction Flow
modules.content: Follow the precise path of energy. Trigger the reaction to watch sunlight transform into physical sugar.

steps.title: 1. Light Absorption
steps.desc: Chlorophyll captures solar energy. Water (H2O) is split into oxygen and protons.

steps.title: 2. Energy Transfer
steps.desc: The electron transport chain charges up temporary battery molecules: ATP and NADPH.

steps.title: 3. The Calvin Cycle
steps.desc: The cell uses the ATP battery power to stitch Carbon Dioxide (CO2) into solid Glucose.

hubs.title: Neural Control & Coordination
hubs.description: The high-speed electrical communication network of the human body.

modules.title: Action Potential Flowchart
modules.content: A high-level systems view of how voltage changes inside a neuron to fire a nerve impulse.
modules.chartDef:
stateDiagram-v2
 direction TB
 [*] --> RestingState : -70mV
 RestingState --> Depolarization : Stimulus (Na+ influx)
 state "Action Potential Fired" as AP {
 Depolarization --> Peak : Reaches +30mV
 }
 AP --> Repolarization : K+ efflux
 Repolarization --> Hyperpolarization : Overshoot (-90mV)
 Hyperpolarization --> RestingState : Na+/K+ Pump restores balance

modules.title: Synaptic Transmission
modules.content: Watch how an electrical signal is converted into a chemical signal to cross the synaptic cleft.
steps: 1. Action potential arrives at axon terminal.
2. Synaptic vesicles fuse with the membrane.
3. Neurotransmitters are released into the cleft.
4. Receptors trigger the next electrical impulse.

hubs.title: Endocrine Control Network
hubs.description: Explore the body's chemical messaging system and hormonal feedback loops.

modules.title: Thyroid Feedback Loop
modules.content: How the brain and thyroid communicate to regulate the body's baseline metabolism.
modules.chartDef:
stateDiagram-v2
 direction TB
 Hypothalamus --> Pituitary_Gland : Releases TRH
 Pituitary_Gland --> Thyroid_Gland : Releases TSH
 Thyroid_Gland --> Target_Cells : Thyroxine (T4)
 Target_Cells --> Hypothalamus : Inhibits TRH (Negative Feedback)
 Target_Cells --> Pituitary_Gland : Inhibits TSH (Negative Feedback)

modules.title: Bloodstream & Receptors
modules.content: Not all hormones work the same way. Select a hormone type to see how it interacts with a target cell.

options.name: Protein Hormone (Water-Soluble)
options.desc: Binds to surface receptors. Cannot pass through the lipid membrane.

options.name: Steroid Hormone (Lipid-Soluble)
options.desc: Phases directly through the membrane to alter DNA in the nucleus.

modules.title: Phagocytosis Battlefield
modules.content: Deploy a Macrophage (white blood cell) to hunt down and digest a viral pathogen in real-time.

hubs.description: Master the biochemical engine of the planet: Photosynthesis.

modules.title: Photosynthesis Engine

hubs.title: Cellular Respiration
hubs.description: Dive deep into the metabolic pathways that generate cellular energy.

modules.title: The Krebs Cycle
modules.content: Follow the carbon atoms as they are oxidized to produce ATP, NADH, and FADH2 in the mitochondrial matrix.
